pattern: refinanc\w*[^.]{0,60}house you are buying|house you are buying[^.]{0,80}refinanc
struck: Cash from refinancing the house you are buying cannot count as its reserves.
use: Cash taken out in a cash-out refinance cannot count toward the reserves for that same refinance.

pattern: (home|house) you live in,? and buy(ing)? another
struck: Renting out the home you live in and buying another: the lender counts three quarters of its market rent.
use: Renting out the home you live in when you buy a new home to live in: the lender counts three quarters of its market rent.

struck: Plus a share of what you owe on your other financed rentals.
use: Plus a share of what you owe on your other financed homes, not counting your own home and the new one.

pattern: HUD's rent[^.]{0,80}lender counts|lender counts about \$?1,6[67]\d of it
struck: HUD's rent for a 3-bedroom in that ZIP is $2,230 a month; the lender counts about $1,670 of it.
use: If the appraiser's rent schedule came in at $2,230, HUD's figure for a 3-bedroom in that ZIP, the lender would count about $1,670.

struck: Landlord insurance about $3,300 a year (one agency's estimate); about $767 a month, $9,200 a year.
use: (cut the insurance figure: tax and dues about $5,900 a year, about $492 a month; insurance is the reader's own quote)

struck: The standard rule asks you to keep about $10,100 plus six months of the new loan's principal and interest.
use: The standard rule asks you to keep about $8,400, plus six months of the new loan's payment and insurance.

struck: Both houses empty for three months: about $4,600 in tax, insurance and dues.
use: Both houses empty for three months: about $2,950 in tax and dues, plus three payments on each loan.

pattern: not the six loan payments|unless they are no larger
struck: It covers that three-month double vacancy's tax, insurance and dues with about $5,500 left, but not the six loan payments on two loans unless they are no larger than the new loan's six.
use: Three empty months on both houses take about $2,950 of that in tax and dues, plus three payments on each loan.

struck: A legal residence rented out more than 72 days in a year loses the 4 percent rate.
use: A legal residence rented out more than 72 days in a calendar year loses the 4 percent rate (active-duty military on orders keep it).

struck: 257 buyers recorded two or more Horry County home purchases: 126 people and 131 companies. Together they bought 650 homes. 193 of them bought exactly two.
use: 255 buyers recorded two or more Horry County home purchases: 138 people and 117 companies. Together they bought 645 homes. 192 of them bought exactly two.

struck: Half of those homes now send the tax bill outside South Carolina.
use: Of those homes the buyers still own, half send the tax bill outside South Carolina.

struck: 6,070 people and companies own two or more homes taxed at the 6 percent rate. 4,091 own exactly two. 3,563 of the 6,070 are people. They hold 23,290 homes.
use: About 6,000 people and companies own two or more homes taxed at the 6 percent rate, not counting resort and timeshare firms. About 4,100 own exactly two. About 4,200 are people, some through a family trust.

struck: Of 3,563 houses with 3 or more bedrooms for sale in Horry County, 67 ask $195,000 or less; of 1,897 condos with 2 or more bedrooms, 432 do.
use: (not on the page: listing counts change daily; the homes strip shows the homes)

pattern: second[- ]home[^.]{0,80}\b(must not|may not|cannot|can't|is not allowed to) be (run as |used as )?(a )?rental( property)?\b
struck: On a second-home loan the home must not be rental property, you must use it part of the year.
use: On a second-home loan the home must not be run mainly as a rental, you must use it part of the year, and any rent it earns cannot help you qualify.

pattern: no new cash|without (any )?new cash|no (cash|money) (out of|from) (your )?savings|nothing (out of|from) (your )?savings
struck: Equity in a home you own can pay toward the next one, so the next purchase needs no new cash from savings.
use: Equity in a home you own can pay toward the next down payment, through a cash-out refinance or a line of credit.

struck: In 2025, lenders reported 3,002 applications for loans on Horry County rentals and made 1,903 loans.
use: In 2025, lenders reported 3,002 applications for loans on Horry County homes the borrower would not live in, rentals and homes bought to resell, and made 1,903 loans.

struck: A line of credit on a rental is rare here.
use: In 2025, lenders reported 17 lines of credit on Horry County investment homes, 149 cash-out refinances on them, and 1,228 lines of credit on homes their owners live in.

pattern: not on rentals|lines? of credit (that )?lenders (here )?(make|put|write) (is|are) on the home
struck: Lenders here put lines of credit on homes people live in, not on rentals.
use: Lines of credit and cash-out refinances lenders reported in Horry County in 2025.

pattern: lines? of credit on (rentals|investment homes) (were|are) (turned down|denied) more often than
struck: Lines of credit on rentals were turned down more often than they were made.
use: Of 56 applications for a line of credit on an investment home that lenders reported deciding in 2025, 35 were turned down, about 6 in 10.

struck: Few lenders offer it: 13 lenders made the 17 rental lines of credit in 2025.
use: 13 lenders reported making the 17 lines of credit on investment homes in 2025.

pattern: next (came|come|is|are)[^.]{0,40}debt[^.]{0,80}\b(and|then)\b[^.]{0,40}(not enough cash|insufficient cash|cash for the down payment)
struck: Next came debt-to-income (65) and not enough cash for the down payment and closing costs (36).
use: Debt compared with income came next, in 65. Not enough cash for the down payment and closing costs was named in 36.

struck: Almost nobody here reaches the ten-home limit: about 170 owners in Horry County hold ten or more homes taxed at the 6 percent rate.
use: About 170 people and companies, not counting resort and timeshare firms, hold ten or more Horry County homes taxed at the 6 percent rate.

struck: The example's $2,230 is about $500 more than HUD's 3-bedroom figure in central Myrtle Beach's ZIP, 29577 ($1,720).
use: The example's $2,230 is about $500 more than HUD's 3-bedroom figure for 29577, Myrtle Beach's main ZIP ($1,720).

struck: Fannie Mae is one of the two companies that buy standard loans from lenders, and this is its rule.
use: Fannie Mae is one of two companies created by Congress that buy home loans from lenders, and this is its rule.

struck: A cash-out refinance is a new, larger loan that pays off the old one and gives you the difference in cash.
use: A cash-out refinance is a new, larger loan that pays off the old one; what is left after closing costs comes to you in cash.
